subject: technology
essential_question: When two algorithms both work, what makes one of them better?
standards: Michigan Computer Science: Algorithms and Programming
project_brief: Compare searching and sorting approaches using complexity reasoning together with measured runtime evidence. This is the grade 10 culminating project for "Algorithms, Efficiency, and Correctness" (ma-g10-technology-u02, unit 2), built around searching algorithms, sorting algorithms, recursion and base cases, complexity and growth rates, and correctness arguments and invariants. Compare searching and sorting approaches using complexity reasoning together with measured runtime evidence. As you build this, trace through your logic by hand for at least one representative input or scenario before you run or finalize it, so you can compare your prediction with the actual result.

remediation: If the project stalls, step back to the smallest version of the task: rebuild just the part covering searching algorithms in isolation, using a worked example from this unit as a model, then re-attach it to the full project once that smaller piece works and you can explain why.
extension: Once the core project is working, extend it to handle a new constraint or edge case related to sorting algorithms, or compare two different approaches to the same problem and explain the real tradeoff between them in your own words.
